notes: Written by hand against the 50-recipe corpus, before any graph existed. Stage 7 has to reproduce these answers; it does not get to define them.
appears_in is the number of the 50 recipes whose ingredient names contain the token. scripts/validate.py recomputes every count and fails if one is wrong.
removes_tags is the field that makes a swap queryable. Replacing ghee with oil only answers a dairy-free question because this records that it removes dairy.
Every alternative carries a tradeoff. A swap with no downside usually means nobody looked properly.

alternatives.name: unsalted butter
alternatives.tradeoff: Burns at a lower temperature, so it will not take a hot tempering.

alternatives.name: vegetable oil
alternatives.tradeoff: Loses the nutty aroma that is the reason most of these recipes ask for ghee.

alternatives.name: coconut oil
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds a coconut note, which suits the South Indian dishes and fights the North Indian ones.

alternatives.name: cilantro
alternatives.tradeoff: None. The same plant under a different name, which is why it is also in the synonym list.

alternatives.name: parsley
alternatives.tradeoff: Looks right and tastes wrong. A last resort.

alternatives.name: cinnamon and a clove
alternatives.tradeoff: Warmer and heavier; loses the floral top note.

alternatives.name: jaggery
alternatives.tradeoff: Darker colour and a mineral edge. Traditional in several of these dishes anyway.

alternatives.name: honey
alternatives.tradeoff: Not vegan, and it scorches where sugar would caramelise.

alternatives.name: coconut milk
alternatives.tradeoff: Much richer and unmistakably coconut. Works in kheer, wrong in chai.

alternatives.name: almond milk
alternatives.tradeoff: Thin, and it introduces nuts - so it does not help a nut-free cook.

alternatives.name: oat milk
alternatives.tradeoff: Closest in body, but it brings gluten.

alternatives.name: red chilli powder
alternatives.tradeoff: Heat without the fresh, grassy flavour. Use roughly a quarter as much.

alternatives.name: paprika
alternatives.tradeoff: Colour and almost no heat. For someone who wants the look, not the burn.

alternatives.name: buttermilk
alternatives.tradeoff: Thinner, so it will not hold a marinade on meat.

alternatives.name: coconut yogurt
alternatives.tradeoff: Sweeter than it should be, and it will not tenderise the way dairy does.

alternatives.name: cashew cream
alternatives.tradeoff: Rich and neutral, but adds nuts.

alternatives.name: desiccated coconut
alternatives.tradeoff: Needs soaking in warm water first or it stays gritty in a chutney.

alternatives.name: omit them
alternatives.tradeoff: There is no substitute. Bay leaf is often suggested and tastes nothing like it, so leaving them out is the more honest answer.

alternatives.name: cassia bark
alternatives.tradeoff: Coarser and more bitter. Usually what is sold as cinnamon anyway.

alternatives.name: cashews
alternatives.tradeoff: Softer and sweeter; still a nut, so no help to a nut-free cook.

alternatives.name: sunflower seeds
alternatives.tradeoff: Grinds to a paste well but tastes greener and less sweet.

alternatives.name: melon seeds
alternatives.tradeoff: The traditional thickener for exactly this job. Harder to find.

alternatives.name: lime
alternatives.tradeoff: Sharper and more floral. Interchangeable in practice.

alternatives.name: tamarind
alternatives.tradeoff: Sour in a deeper, fruitier way, and it darkens the dish.

alternatives.name: ghee
alternatives.tradeoff: Still dairy. Takes more heat without burning.

alternatives.name: vegetable oil
alternatives.tradeoff: No creaminess, which is most of the point in butter chicken.

alternatives.name: chopped dates
alternatives.tradeoff: Stickier and sweeter; will not plump in hot ghee the same way.

alternatives.name: coriander leaves
alternatives.tradeoff: None. Same plant.

alternatives.name: rice flour
alternatives.tradeoff: Will not form gluten, so a dough made with it cannot be rolled thin without tearing.

alternatives.name: besan
alternatives.tradeoff: Strong flavour of its own. Right for a batter, wrong for a flatbread.

alternatives.name: blanched almonds
alternatives.tradeoff: Firmer, so it grinds less smoothly. Still a nut.

alternatives.name: sunflower seeds
alternatives.tradeoff: Loses the buttery texture that makes a cashew chutney worth making.

alternatives.name: lemon juice
alternatives.tradeoff: Brighter and thinner. Add at the end rather than cooking it down.

alternatives.name: amchoor
alternatives.tradeoff: Dry mango powder. Sour without the body tamarind gives a sambar.

alternatives.name: lemon
alternatives.tradeoff: Slightly rounder and less sharp.

alternatives.name: paneer
alternatives.tradeoff: Makes the dish vegetarian but adds dairy, so it does not help a vegan. Add it late; it does not need cooking.

alternatives.name: cauliflower
alternatives.tradeoff: Takes the sauce well and gives up none of its own richness, because it has none.

alternatives.name: firm tofu
alternatives.tradeoff: Needs pressing and browning first or it falls apart in a long braise.

alternatives.name: dark brown sugar
alternatives.tradeoff: Close. Slightly less mineral, slightly sweeter.

alternatives.name: a little garlic and onion powder
alternatives.tradeoff: Covers the savoury gap but not the sulphurous top note. Most commercial asafoetida is cut with wheat flour, so check it if gluten matters.

alternatives.name: masoor dal
alternatives.tradeoff: Cooks faster and breaks down further, so a sambar made with it is thinner.

alternatives.name: moong dal
alternatives.tradeoff: Lighter and sweeter; loses the earthiness.

alternatives.name: channa dal
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine as a tempering crunch, but it will not ferment, so no dosa batter.

notes: A mood is a structural claim, never a keyword search. 'Cooling' is not recipes whose text contains the word cooling; it is recipes built on yogurt, cucumber or coconut milk.
Constraints combine with AND. Each list means 'at least one of these'. Written this way so the predicate is unambiguous and can be recomputed by anyone.

recipe_ids is filled in by scripts/build_golden_artefacts.py from the predicate, then committed. Stage 7's Cypher has to reproduce this list. It does not get to define it - that circularity is exactly what made the previous version score 1.000 and prove nothing.
These definitions are opinions about food, openly held. Disagreeing with one is a disagreement about the definition, not evidence that retrieval failed - which is why each thin one carries a caveat.

moods.definition: Something warm and filling. A main, rice or bread dish carrying dairy or wheat.
A short ingredient list and a course that is not the centre of the meal.
moods.caveat: Uses ingredient count as a proxy for lightness, which is crude. A short list can still be deep-fried.

moods.definition: The book states a total time and it is half an hour or less.
moods.caveat: Decided on the 34 of 50 recipes with a recoverable duration. total_time_minutes alone is stated by the book for far fewer, so effective_time_minutes falls back to the sum of timed steps.

moods.definition: Built around the expensive things: saffron, nuts and dried fruit.
Chilli or peppercorn is doing the work.
moods.caveat: Presence is not quantity. A pinch of pepper and six red chillies both match, and the corpus rarely gives enough detail to tell them apart.

moods.definition: Yogurt, cucumber or coconut milk as the base - the dishes served against heat.
Six ingredients or fewer, and none of them meat, fish or nuts.
moods.caveat: Counts ingredients, not cost. Saffron in a four-item list would still qualify.
